name: Non-acquired Combined Pituitary Hormone Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Pituitary Hormone Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Deficiency of two or more anterior pituitary hormones confirmed by biochemical testing
MRI evidence of pituitary hypoplasia or structural abnormalities of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis
Presence of clinical features consistent with hormone deficiencies such as growth retardation, hypothyroidism, or adrenal insufficiency
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with pituitary development (e.g., PROP1, POU1F1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Biochemical confirmation of deficiency of at least two anterior pituitary hormones plus MRI evidence of pituitary or hypothalamic abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe growth hormone deficiency with growth retardation
searchTerms: poor growth due to hormone deficiency

pathognomonic.symptomName: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to ACTH deficiency
searchTerms: low adrenal function from ACTH deficiency
adrenal hormone shortage due to pituitary

common.symptomName: Delayed or absent puberty due to gonadotropin deficiency
searchTerms: puberty failure due to hormone deficiency
low blood sugar episodes in babies

common.symptomName: Fatigue and weakness related to hormone deficiencies
searchTerms: tiredness and weakness from hormone lack

common.symptomName: Poor feeding and failure to thrive in infants
searchTerms: infant feeding difficulties and growth delay
low blood pressure from adrenal insufficiency
feeling cold due to low thyroid
poor cold tolerance with thyroid issues

occasional.symptomName: Headache related to pituitary mass effect
searchTerms: head pain due to pituitary swelling

occasional.symptomName: Visual field defects due to pituitary stalk or hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: partial vision loss due to brain lesion

rare.symptomName: Hyponatremia due to secondary adrenal insufficiency
searchTerms: low blood sodium from adrenal insufficiency
seizures caused by low blood sugar

laboratory: Low serum levels of pituitary hormones (GH, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH, prolactin)
Low target gland hormones (cortisol, free T4, sex steroids)
imaging: MRI showing hypoplastic or absent anterior pituitary
genetic: Mutations in PROP1, POU1F1, HESX1, LHX3, LHX4 genes
other: Abnormal stimulation tests for pituitary hormones

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma, infection, tumor, or radiation
Later onset after infancy or childhood
Deficiency limited to growth hormone only
Normal levels of other pituitary hormones

redFlags: Severe hypoglycemia in neonates or infants
Failure to thrive with multiple hormone deficiencies
references: Caron P, et al. Combined pituitary hormone deficiency: clinical, genetic, and molecular aspects. Endocr Rev. 2020;41(3):1-25.
